title: Endless Stair
concept: A Shepard-Risset glissando of nine octave-spaced sines under a Gaussian loudness bell, seen as a log spiral that turns one revolution per octave so the endless rise becomes an endless zoom.

mechanism_embodied.how_visualised: Nine copper beads ride a log spiral outward, one turn per octave; their size and level follow the Gaussian bell, so the outermost fades as a newborn bead appears at the centre. The spectral ribbon below shows the same hand-off on a log-frequency axis.

discarded_obvious_idea: A barber-pole stripe animation next to the sound: it shows that something loops but not why, with no partials and no loudness envelope.
motion_sound_plan: Sound starts on the first click or key press and never before. Nine sines from 27.5 Hz, an octave apart, rise at 0.2 octave per second under a Gaussian bell over log-frequency, through a gentle delay, compressor and soft limiter. Visually, the spiral counter-turns with the pitch so the rise reads as an endless zoom.

storyboard.description: A Shepard scale: twelve semitone steps, the spiral jumping one tick per step.
The steps melt into Risset's continuous glide; the spiral zooms without end.
The spiral stops turning, and the beads are seen riding outward along it, fading at the rim and born at the centre.
The loudness bell widens on the ring and the ribbon, so the partials at the edges come forward and the seam starts to show.

memorable_moment: The moment the spiral stops and the endless zoom is revealed as beads quietly handing off at the rim and the centre.
self_declared_risk: On small laptop speakers the lowest partials vanish and the bell sounds lopsided, weakening the illusion.
liner_note: Roger Shepard found that sine waves spaced an octave apart, with the lowest and highest faded out, seem to rise forever when shifted up together: after an octave the sound is the same as at the start. Jean-Claude Risset made the steps into a continuous glide. Here, nine sines from 27.5 Hz rise at a fifth of an octave per second under a fixed Gaussian loudness bell. The picture is the same model: a log spiral with one turn per octave, so a full turn equals a zoom by two. Click or press a key for sound.
